title: Relative rational maps and birational self-map charts
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X,Y$ be schemes over $S$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. An open $U\subset X$ is $S$-dense if its inverse image in every fibre $X_s$ is topologically dense. A relative partial map $X\dashrightarrow Y$ is an $S$-morphism from an $S$-dense open of $X$ to $Y$. Two such maps agree if their restrictions agree as scheme morphisms on an $S$-dense common open; a relative rational map is a class modulo this relation. A birational self-map chart of $X$ is an isomorphism over $S$ between two $S$-dense opens of $X$. Birational self-maps are charts modulo agreement on an $S$-dense common open. For charts $f,g,h$, the predicate that $h=f\circ g$ means there is an $S$-dense open $H$ in the domains of $g$ and $h$, and a morphism $v:H\to\operatorname{dom}(f)$ whose composite with the domain inclusion is $g|_H$ and whose composite with $f$ is $h|_H$. For $Y/S$ and a base morphism $g:T'\to T$, a chart over $T'$ is the pullback of a chart over $T$ if its two opens are the full inverse images under the canonical map $Y_{T'}\to Y_T$, and its isomorphism is the pullback isomorphism (the maps of both open subschemes and the isomorphisms commute).
